scenarios.label: front-load then taper: 22h through day 13, 12h from day 14, Sundays on

taper.derived_note: phase ceilings and the switch day are derived from the scenario's own day files, never typed

scenarios.label: 12h shifts, Sundays on
scenarios.note: the cheapest lever — same shift, Sundays on; Sunday wages are NOT modelled

takeaway: The front-load-then-taper question, answered by the same engine: taper to 12h after day 13 and the month keeps only 45.6% of the flat-22h gain; taper to 18h after day 13 and 84.1% of that gain survives on 80% of flat-22h's extra hours. Flat 24h remains max output; plain Sundays-on (12h × 30d) remains the best hours-to-litres conversion at 82.7%.
method_note: pct_extra_hours_used = (line-hours used beyond baseline) / (extra line-hours offered); offered = scenario available line-hours − baseline available line-hours, where available = shift ceiling × working days × number of lines, and a tapered pattern uses its per-phase ceilings (front through the switch day, tail after) derived from its own day files; every figure computed from the scenario artifacts
artifact_note: every pattern shown has a full 30-day artifact on disk (summary, day files, events) — including the 18h-tail taper an earlier build flagged as missing
